L98: Since subharmonic functions are stable under decreasing limits, and the psh functions are defined by a transfinite regularization process from smooth psh functions, it is enough to show that a smooth psh function on $C$ is subharmonic. This follows from a result of Wanner [【49†Wan19】, Theorem 4.7].
L99: ### 1.3. Plurisubharmonic ${\mathbf{R}}$-PL functions
L100: For an ${\mathbf{R}}$-piecewise linear function $h\colon X\to{\mathbf{R}}$ on a good strictly $k$-analytic space over a non-trivially valued field $k$, we have studied the notion of semipositivity in the paper [【50†GR25】]. This notion is a local analytic version of the global semipositive metrics introduced by Zhang [【42†Zha95】] which are induced by nef models. We show in Theorem 【31†4】 that an ${\mathbf{R}}$-PL function $h$ is semipositive if and only if $h$ is classically psh.
L101: ### 1.4. Connectivity by curves
L102: In Theorem 【32†5】, we show that two points $x,y$ of a connected $k$-analytic space $X$ can be connected by analytic curves (assumed to be compact and defined over a non-Archimedean field extension of $k$). If $\partial X=\emptyset$, then we even show that $x,y$ can be connected by overconvergent curves, which means roughly speaking that we can connect them with the interiors of compact curves. We refer to Section 【32†5】 for the precise definitions.
L103: The proof of Theorem 【32†5】 is inspired by Berkovich’s proof [【51†Ber90】, §3.2] showing that a connected $k$-analytic space is pathwise connected. However, we have to choose different paths, as the ones in ibid are not analytic curves. This result is related to [【52†dJ95】, Proposition 6.1.1] and [【53†Ber07】, Theorem 4.1.1] (see the discussion after the statement of Theorem 【32†5】 for more details).
L104: ###### Theorem \the\thmnumbering (Local Maximum Principle).
L105: 
L106: Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space, and let $u$ be a classically psh function on $X$. If $u$ has a local maximum on $x\in\operatorname{Int}(X)$, then $u$ is locally constant at $x$.
L107: 
L108: This will be shown in Theorem 【33†6】. For the proof, one may assume that $\partial X=\emptyset$; then we reduce the claim to the local maximum principle for $k$-analytic curves using connectivity by overconvergent curves.
L545: As explained in [【95†BPR13】, Theorem 4.6] (see also [【96†BL85】, Propositions 2.2 and 2.3]), if $\xi$ is a generic point then $\operatorname{red}^{-1}(\xi)$ is a single type-$2$ point of $X$; if $\xi$ is a smooth closed point then $\operatorname{red}^{-1}(\xi)$ is isomorphic to an open unit ball; and if $\xi$ is a node then $\operatorname{red}^{-1}(\xi)$ is isomorphic to an open annulus. In particular, if $\xi$ is a closed point then $\operatorname{red}^{-1}(\xi)$ is connected and open.
L763: This result can be found in different forms in the literature. De Jong proves in [【52†dJ95】, Proposition 6.1.1] that any two rig-points of a strictly $k$-analytic space over a discretely valued field can be connected by strictly $k$-affinoid curves. Berkovich proves in [【53†Ber07】, Theorem 4.1.1] that any two rig-points in a connected, boundaryless $k$-analytic space (for arbitrary $k$) can be connected by boundaryless $k$-analytic curves (of a special type).
